course_description:
This course continues and completes the readings from JACT Reading Greek: Text and Vocabulary, sections 16-20.

GREK3000 is a two-unit (#2) course, which emphasizes reading skills and builds gradually upon the basic grammar and syntax of classical Greek learnt in GREK2230. GREK3000 finishes the remaining sections (16C-20G)ﾠof the JACT ﾠ Reading Greek textbook which include the translation ofﾠpassages from Plato, Herodotus and Homer. Once the JACT readings are concluded, we will go on to analyse and translateﾠAndokides On the Mysteries. ﾠThere are 3 hours of classes per week. As with learning any language, regular attendance and study are vitally important.

learning_outcomes.description: read a range of passages in Ancient Greek containing the parts of speech and syntax covered in the JACT Reading Greek course.
translate into good English a range of passages covered in the JACT Reading Greek course and extracts from related authors outside of the JACT textbook.
recognise and classify a range of different parts of speech.
parse (give the grammatical properties of) various parts of speech covered in the JACT Reading Greek course.
appreciate some of the distinctive features of the studied authors in their historical and social context.

assessment_details.task_description: The participation mark evaluates student preparedness demonstrated through in-class translation of set lines and active engagement in discussions directed by the lecturer. These discussions will focus on points of grammar, literary technique, and relevant literary, historical or cultural contexts. Students are encouraged to use the class time to identify and address problems encountered during preparation proactively. Although AI and Machine translation can be used for this task, it does not help students to master the skills needed, and in some cases may be misleading and potentially more time-consuming. Nor will advanced reading, analysis and comprehension skills be developed and mastered unless students translate and understand the Greek texts yourself. assessment_details.due_date: 5/10/2026 - 26/10/2026 Please submit your Part A: Translation and Analysis through the Turnitin submission link on Blackboard.
assessment_details.task_description: PART A Translation and Analysis and PART B oral presentation of a passage from Andocides' On the Mysteries PART A: Written Component (20%) Task: Write a detailed commentary on an allocated passage from Andocides' On the Mysteries . Your commentary should include: A complete and accurate translation of the passages. In-depth analysis of the 5 key features identified in your oral presentation, supported by evidence from the text [approximately 200-300 words each]. Submit your commentary to Turnitin by the due date. Part B: Oral Component (5%) Task: Present an oral translation and analysis of an allocated passage from Andocides' On the Mysteries . Recite the Greek text first, followed by your English translation. Discuss 5 key features of the passage, such as: Word choice Points of grammar Grammatical and literary constructions Historical references Historical context Legal issues Mythological references Other relevant aspects Foster class discussion by asking questions and encouraging participation. Use a PowerPoint or other visual aids to enhance your presentation if you wish. Note: Please ensure that your oral and written components align and complement each other. Your commentary should provide a more in-depth analysis of the features discussed in your presentation.
